text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PROD deploy alert: redwood-service canary error rate > 8% (us-west-2). Triggered by pipeline #5824. Paging on-call

sasha_ops: seeing the same in datadog - 5xx spike on /generate (canary pods only)

manny_build: I just watched the canary deploy from CI. The artifact tag looks off, pipeline used 'latest' fallback after digest lookup failed in staging cache.

katy_oncall: on it, taking primary. @manny_build can you paste the pipeline job log?

manny_build: log excerpt:
```
[2024-11-02T14:02:11Z] resolving image artifact -> query cache
[2024-11-02T14:02:11Z] cache miss for digest, falling back to tag: redwood-service:latest
[2024-11-02T14:02:12Z] pushing image to canary pool -> OK
[2024-11-02T14:02:13Z] deploy started to us-west-2 canary (replicas=3)
[2024-11-02T14:03:01Z] healthchecks failing 2/3 pods
```

platform-eng-ryan: that matches what I see — the 'latest' image includes an old config that turns on the structured-logging experiment and a flag that the service can't handle in canary mode, causing NPEs.

katy_oncall: customer impact? pm-olivia?

pm-olivia: minor impact so far: a handful of premium tenants hitting errors (~1% of traffic routed to canary). Monitoring alert noise for a few customers; nothing escalated to SRE yet.

cust-sre-ivy: got two support tickets about 500s from EU customers hitting the degraded path (they were routed to us-west canary via caching). Investigating if any latency-sensitive flows retried.

sasha_ops: next steps — stop rollout + flip feature flag kill-switch for canary routing. I'll attempt kill-switch first so we can avoid full rollback.

katy_oncall: agree. How do we flip the flag quickly? We have FF service endpoint and LD fallback.

platform-eng-ryan: internal flag endpoint: POST /flags/canary-routing/redwood-service with {enabled: false}. I'm pasting the curl we use in emergencies:
```bash
curl -s -X POST \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET_OPS_TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  https://flags.internal/api/v1/flags/canary-routing/redwood-service \ 
  -d '{"enabled": false, "actor":"oncall/katy"}'
```

sasha_ops: executed kill-switch at 14:05:42 UTC. Response: 200 OK, new state: disabled. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Automatically rerouting traffic away from canary. Expected convergence in ~30s.

sasha_ops: checking ingress logs — 30s later traffic back to stable pool, errors dropping.

manny_build: since the pipeline fell back to 'latest' due to digest resolution failing, we should mark the build as flaky and pin to digest for canary deploys. I opened a quick PR to the pipeline to fail on cache miss: https://ci.internal/pipelines/5824/changeset/patch-1

katy_oncall: good. Is a rollback still needed or kill-switch sufficient?

platform-eng-ryan: kill-switch mitigated immediate customer impact. But artifact in registry is tainted; we should roll back canary to the previous stable digest to be safe and then re-run CI with a fixed cache resolution.

manny_build: rollback command I'm going to run (kubectl):
```bash
kubectl -n prod set image deployment/redwood-service redwood-service=registry.redwood.ai/redwood-service@sha256:aa11bb22cc33 --record
kubectl -n prod rollout status deployment/redwood-service
```

katy_oncall: Manny, coordinate with platform to run rollback only on canary subset first. We don't want a full prod rollback if the canary was isolated.

platform-eng-ryan: I'll scope rollout to node selector used by canary pool. Running now.

incident-bot: rollback job started by platform-eng-ryan at 14:12:10 UTC.

manny_build: rollback finished at 14:15:05 UTC. Canary pods now running digest aa11bb22cc33, healthchecks pass.

katy_oncall: monitoring shows errors resolved. Metrics back to baseline.

pm-olivia: updating customers: sent templated note to affected premium tenants explaining transient canary issue, steps we took, and mitigation.

cust-sre-ivy: support tickets updated and closed with root-cause summary.

katy_oncall: post-incident actions: (1) change pipeline to fail on digest cache miss (manny will PR), (2) add an automated check to CI that prevents 'latest' fallback in deploy job, (3) add runbook step for flipping canary routing flag and a token rotation for ops token used in curl. I'll assign follow-ups.

manny_build: PR #834 opened to error on cache miss + better logging. Link: https://ci.internal/pipelines/5824/PR-834

platform-eng-ryan: will add a canary policy gate to console to show when deploy used tag vs digest.

katy_oncall: handoff: I'm passing to @sasha_ops for post-incident writeup and follow-up owners. I'm out at 15:00 UTC.

sasha_ops: taking post-incident, will create postmortem draft and link everyone. Thanks all. :coffee:

incident-bot: Incident resolved by katy_oncall at 14:20:48 UTC. Severity: Sev2 -> downgraded.
